summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Zong Rinpoche studied at Ganden Shartse and Gyuto Monasteries under Dechen Nyingpo and Trijang Rinpoche. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse Monastery (1937–1946) and Director and Rektor at CIHTS (1965–1971).

Specializing in philosophy and sinology, Mou studied at Peking University under Shili Xiong. He held posts at Tunghai University (~1956–1968), CUHK (~1968–1974), New Asia College (1968–1974), and New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (~1974–1995).

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gelle studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Teacher Training College, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna. She held posts at Dharma Gate Buddhist College, the University of Vienna (2011–2014), and ELTE (2014–2016).
Specializing in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies, Tachibana studied under Kozui Otani (~1907–1914) and Edward Denison Ross (~1913–1914).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Ito completed degrees at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo. He lectured at Shinshu, Waseda, and Tokyo universities, and served as professor of Buddhist studies at Rissho University (1980–2013).
A Buddhist studies scholar, Goto studied at the Second Higher School, the University of Tokyo (1903–1906), and under Sokatsu Shaku (~1900–1914). He served as president of Hanazono University in 1932.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Yamaguchi studied at the University of Tokyo, EPHE, and under Jacques Bacot and Rolf Alfred Stein. He worked at CNRS, Toyo Bunko, the University of Tokyo (1970–1986), and Nagoya University (1986).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Nakamura studied under Susumu Yamaguchi in 1944 and became a Professor of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University in 1945.
Gyurme tubten nyinje studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Pad+ma la studied under Dilgo Khyentse and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Specializing in sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, Chavannes studied at the ENS, Collège de France, and INALCO under Marie-Jean-Léon d'Hervey de Saint Denys and Maurice Jametel. He served as professor at the Collège de France (1893–1918).

A scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Huber studied at the Sorbonne, University of Paris, Collège de France, and under Sylvain Lévi and Johann Baptist Schibenegg. He taught Chinese at the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (1901–1905).
Reclus studied at the Faculté libre de théologie protestante de Montauban (1848–1849) and held a post at the New University of Brussels (~1894–1905).

Specializing in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Benveniste studied at the University of Paris and EPHE under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held chairs at EPHE (1927–1969) and the Collège de France (1937–1969).
A philosopher, Chartier completed his studies at Lycée Pierre-Corneille (~1881–1886) and the École Normale Supérieure (~1889–1892).

A scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology, Chatelain studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1872–1876). He held posts at the École française de Rome (1876–1877) and the EPHE (~1881–1926).

A scholar of religious studies and other fields, Durkheim studied at the ENS and University of Leipzig under Wilhelm Wundt. He held posts at the University of Bordeaux (1887–1902) and as professor at the Sorbonne (~1902–1917).

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, Senart studied at Göttingen and Munich under Theodor Benfey. He served as a professor at the Collège de France and as president of the Société Asiatique (1908–1928).

A scholar of Indology and linguistics, Burnouf studied at the ENS and University of Paris under Jean-Louis and Eugène Burnouf. He served as director of the École française d'Athènes (1867–1875) and professor at the University of Nancy (~1867–1878).

A scholar of sinology, history, and archaeology, Balazs studied under Otto Franke (1923–1930). He held posts at the CNRS (1949) and as a professor of Chinese economic history at the University of Paris (~1955–1963).
